4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement and contended, inter-alia that Gobinda Bairagi had although in passion of the suit land. He was married and dies leaving only one son and heir Bishweshwar Bairagi, who sold the said land to the defendant No. 1 by kabala dated 10.8.1972 and delivered possession of the suit land to him. The defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land by constructing hats on approved plan from Municipality. Plaintiff's allegation of making the suit land khas by Ambika Charan, the superior owner and settling the land orally by Monindra, Son of Ambika to the plaintiff is absolutely false and the plaintiff never possessed the suit land. The defendant No.1 further contended that the allegation of dispossession by him is also false. 

 5. The trial Court dismissed the suit disbelieving the case of the plaintiff that he had taken oral settlement of the land from Monindra Charan after making the suit land khas by superior landlord and delivered possession the plaintiff and dispossession from the suit land by the defendant No. 1. the trial court has believed that Gobinda Bairagi left his son, Bishashwar as his heir and that Bishashwar legally transferred the suit land to the defendant No. 1. Further, the trial court has held that tenancy of Gobinda Bairagi was not terminated legally and as such alleged settlement of suit land orally to the plaintiff is illegal. It appears that the appellate court believed the possession of the plaintiff, who was allegedly dispossessed by the defendant No. 1 Further appellate court has held that the appellate court believed the possession of the plaintiff, who was allegedly dispossessed by the defendant No. 1 Further appellate court has held that Gobinda Bairagi abandoned his rayoti right and then the landlord Ambika legally made the suit land khas, and his son Monindra settled the suit land orally to the plaintiff after the death of Ambika. The appellate court has relied on two documents, namely, a certificate from the local Chairman marked Ext. X and the voter list of the locality, which were filed for the first time before the appellate court and found that Gobinda Bairagi was unmarried and Bisheshwar was not his son. The High Court Division with regard to the aforesaid two documents has held that these two documents were not legally considered by the appellate Court as the same were not proved in accordance with law, and the same were not admitted as additional evidence in compliance with the provision of order 41, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil procedure, yet the appellate court on the basis of those two documents has held that Gobinda Bairagi was unmarried and Bishashwar was not t his son. The High Court Division has held that the finding on the basis of that evidence is wrong because the said documents were not legally proved. Further, the High Court Division has held that the superior landlord could make the land of a rayoit khash and could take it under his own possession only in compliance of the provision of section 87(1) (2) of the Bengal Tenancy Act but the same was not done in the present case. Sub-sections 1 and 2 of Section 87 of B.T. Act are as under:- 

 "The Bengal Tenancy Act has not given any definition of the word 'abandonment'. But it connotes the idea of a tenant vacating the land with the intention of never returning to it. Mere temporary absence or absence in circumstances which cannot lead to the inference that the tenant had departed from the land without caring as to what hap-pens thereto, this is not sufficient to warrant the inference of abandonment. It was, therefore, necessary to see some more positive acts than mere non-residence to establish abandonment" 

 7. On the basis of the aforesaid provision of law the High Court Division has found that alleged abandonment of the suit land by its tenant Gobinda Bairagi could not be established by the plaintiff and making it khash by the landlord in accordance with law. S.A. Khatian admittedly was prepared in the name of Gobinda Bairagi, therefore, it supports that Gobinda Bairagi did not abandon the suit property and the High Court Division did not believe the contention of the plaintiff that landlord made the land khash and took it under his own possession. Further, the High Court Division has held that address of Gobinda Bairagi at 24, parganas of west Bengal in the S.A. khatian cannot take away his right from the suit property, as abandonment by him could not be established. Record of rights in the case reflects the correct state of affairs and reliance has been placed by the High Court Division in decision reported 9 DLR 467. 

 8. The claim of the plaintiff that he took oral settlement of the suit land. The High Court Division has held that termination of tenancy of Gobinda Bairagi was not made legally. Therefore, whether the settlement was made orally or not is of little significance. In fact, it has no value in the eye of law. Further, the High Court Division has held that proceedings or Rent Suit No. 150 of 1959 has also no impact upon the claim of the plaintiff since it did not reach finality. The High Court Division has held that the defendant admittedly is in possession of the suit land having his huts and homestead on it, It has been held in the case of Lal Miah vs. Hazi Md. Ibrahim reported in 28 DLR 61 that:- 

 10. Before the High. Court Division plaintiff-opposite party referred to the decision reported in 1 DLR (PC) 5 Hurbert James -vs-Golam Hossain Akeema. The High Court Division found that the said decision is not applicable in the present case because the same does not tally either in spirit of facts. Further, the learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that the appellant filed a Criminal Case against the respondent for disturbing his possession under Section 424/448 which proved appellant's possession in the suit land. It appears that the said Criminal Cass was withdrawn. Therefore, the said case has not bearing upon the decision of the present case. Further, it has been held in the case reported in 3 BLD (AD) 334 that finding of Criminal Courts is not binding on the Civil Courts. The High Court Division has gone to say that the important thing in this case is that the defendant is in possession of the suit land and constructed homestead on the basis of the approved plan from the Municipality and unless the plaintiff can prove, better title he cannot get a decree for declaration of his title and for khas possession. The High Court Division has held that the appellate court upon misreading and non-reading of the evidence on record found the possession in favor of the plaintiff and also found that the defendant had dispossessed him. The High Court Division further accepted the view of the trial Court wherein it has been found that since the termination of tenancy of Gobinda Bairagi by his landlord Ambika Charm could not be proved to have been made in accordance with law the plaintiff's title of the suit land falls like pack of cards having no evidentiary value, Further, the High Court Division has held that the plaintiff can only succeed on the material of his own cause and he cannot get a decree on the weakness or failure of the defendants. This view gets support from the decision in the case of Naimuddin Sarder-vs- Abul Kalam reported in 39 DLR (AD) 237. 

 12. The plaintiff being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division moved this Court and obtained the leave mainly on the grounds that the High Court Division failed to consider properly Ext. 2, suit register of Rent Suit No. 150 of 1956 which proves that landlord Manindra admitted Rakhal as the korfa tenant of the suit land by filing the said rent suit and also Ext.3, the enquiry report of the local Tashilder, in Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1968-98 under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950, and Ext. 6 an order of the local circle officer (revenue), for mutating the name of Rakhal on the basis of Ext.3. Further, the High Court Division ought not to have reversed the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate Court as to the possession of the parties in the suit land. 

 15. It appears that the plaintiff's claim is that he took oral settlement of the suit land from Monindra but the plaintiff has failed to adduce any paper with regard to the settlement although he has stated that he lost the papers during the liberation war. The basis of alleged oral settlement has not been substantiated by the plaintiff. Further, the Gobinda Bairagi was admittedly the tenant under the landlord Ambika, who did not take the suit land from the aforesaid Gobinda Bairagi legally who could take it under his possession only in compliance of section 87(1)(2) of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Therefore, the alleged claim of the plaintiff of no substance since the Gobinda Bairagi never abandoned the suit land and the landlord never took the land in compliance with Section 87(1) & (2) of B.T. Act.
